results.name: Jardin des Plantes
results.why_it_is_special: An ancient botanical garden created in 1794 by naturalist Philippe Picot de Lapeyrouse, originally for medical students to study medicinal plants. Offers remarkable trees, themed botanical squares, and seasonal collections.

results.name: Jardin Japonais Pierre-Baudis (Jardin Compans-Caffarelli)
results.locality: Toulouse centre (Boulevard Lascrosses / Boulevard de la Marquette)
results.why_it_is_special: A tranquil Japanese-inspired garden inside the Compans-Caffarelli park featuring a Zen rock garden, Buddhist statues, a tea pavilion, a red bridge, a dragon sculpture, and a shimmering lake — a surprising oasis of exoticism near the old city ramparts.

results.name: Prairie des Filtres
results.locality: Toulouse centre (left bank of the Garonne, between Pont Neuf and Pont Saint-Michel)
results.principal_activities: Picnicking, riverside walking, summer "Toulouse Plage" beach, open-air festivals
results.why_it_is_special: One of the most popular green spaces in the city, stretching along the Garonne with magnificent views of the river and the pink-brick quays of Tounis. Named after the historic water-filtering system that once supplied Toulouse's fountains. Hosts the Rio Loco world-music festival each June.

results.name: Canal du Midi towpath
results.locality: Starts in Toulouse centre, extends southeast toward Avignonet-Lauragais and beyond
results.why_it_is_special: A UNESCO World Heritage waterway lined with plane trees. A 50 km flat, car-free greenway runs from Toulouse to Avignonet-Lauragais on the old towpath — ideal for a half-day or full-day cycling outing. Shorter strolls along the canal within the city are equally rewarding.

results.name: Base de Loisirs de La Ramée
results.locality: Tournefeuille (≈ 10 km west of Toulouse centre)
results.principal_activities: Walking, swimming (summer beach), paddle sports, picnicking, golf
results.why_it_is_special: A 243-hectare outdoor recreation area built around a 44-hectare lake fed by the Canal de Saint-Martory. Includes woodland, play areas, and a public beach with fine sand in summer — a quick escape from the city accessible by bus.

results.name: Lac du Bocage
results.principal_activities: Trail walking, water sports, tennis, picnicking
results.why_it_is_special: A green setting offering trails, water activities, and sports courts — an easy half-day outing from the city centre.

results.name: Lac d'Oô hike (Pyrenees)
results.locality: Granges d'Astau, near Bagnères-de-Luchon (≈ 2 h drive south of Toulouse)
results.principal_activities: Hiking, swimming in a mountain lake, picnicking
results.why_it_is_special: A gentle 6.6 km round-trip hike with about 440 m elevation gain, rated easy-to-moderate and suitable for families. Ends at a stunning mountain lake with a waterfall — the most popular nature destination in the Haute-Garonne Pyrenees. Allow 2½–3 hours for the walk.

results.name: Balnéa Spa & Paragliding (Loudenville valley, Pyrenees)
results.locality: Valley of Loudenville (≈ 2 h south of Toulouse)
results.principal_activities: Outdoor thermal pools, indoor spa, tandem paragliding
results.why_it_is_special: An open-air spa complex with indoor and outdoor pools set against a dramatic Pyrenean mountain backdrop. The same valley is home to paragliding operators offering tandem flights — combine relaxation with an aerial adventure in a single day trip.
